monitors.name: LG 29WK600
monitors.notes: Ignores standard VCP 0x60 writes; switches through LG vendor code 0xF4. Generic capabilities list an extra DisplayPort code the panel does not have. Picture-mode values are advertised in decimal and the list is wrong (it includes 9, 10 and 44, which are not modes on this unit, and omits HDR Effect = 39), so only the 10 known modes are offered. Learned on DESKTOP-BPMFO0B: Sharpness, Super Resolution+ and Buzzer change no DDC code; Color Temp (Warm, in Custom) changed no code in one try. Gamma (0xFE) reads 18 in HDR Effect and its advertised list (00 01 02) is wrong. Toggling FreeSync also changes the value read back on 0xF4. Write-verified (address 0x51): brightness, contrast, volume, picture mode, response time, FreeSync. Gamma and black stabilizer ignore DDC writes in Custom and FPS Game 1, so they are read-only. Color temperature (0x14): writing 6500 K or 9300 K sets the menu's Color Temp to Custom with that temperature; the menu presets Warm, Medium and Cool are not reachable over DDC, 0x14 does not report them, and User 1 (0x0B) is rejected. Red, green and blue only change in the Custom picture modes (Custom and Custom (Game)); the panel hides them in the others. Deep scan + guided check (2026-10-24): black level red/green/blue (0x6C/0x6E/0x70) are not advertised but write, read back, restore and visibly tint blacks, in Custom and in Reader; default 50. Offered only in the Custom picture modes (with red, green and blue), so other modes do not show black levels alone. Sharpness (0x87) is write-only: writes in steps of 10 visibly change the picture (checked by eye, there and back, in Custom, Custom (Game) and even Reader) but DDC and the menu keep reporting 50, so the app remembers the last value; it is offered only in the Custom picture modes, like the monitor's own menu. Color Temp presets (2026-10-25): the menu and DDC show red/green/blue 50/50/50 and 0x14 = 05 for Custom, Warm, Medium and Cool, so presets are not stored as gains; Warm looks the same as 6500 K and Cool the same as 9300 K (0x14 = 08); Medium has no DDC equivalent and 0x0C stays 35. Profiles (2026-10-25): response time written in Reader, Cinema, FPS Game 1 and Photo goes back to the mode's own value (Reader/Cinema 2, FPS Game 1 1) even 3 s after the mode loaded, and 9300 K in Photo reads back 6500 K, so both are adjustable only in the Custom picture modes. 0x14 values are shown as the menu names: 05 = Warm (looks the same as 6500 K), 08 = Cool (9300 K); profiles written with 6500 K / 9300 K still work through the standard color preset names. FreeSync is a gaming feature: offered in the Custom and game picture modes only. Switching FreeSync re-syncs the HDMI link; afterwards the Intel driver no longer found \\.\DISPLAY2 by name until the display was looked up again.
